From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP: Clarification on performance characterization methodology

Tim —

Appreciate the clear list. Ive attached our test plan (PDF) and the raw results CSV. Below is a concise, reproducible description of the harness and the guardrails we used so your team can re-run or map to your environment. If you want an executable script (docker / k8s job) we can provide that under the NDA.

Summary (high level)
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (PCIe) and NVIDIA H100 80GB for select runs. All tests pinned to a single GPU unless noted.
- OS / drivers: Ubuntu 22.04, NVIDIA driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.0, cuBLAS/cuDNN as shipped with the runtime.
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime v2.4.1 (continuous batching enabled), model execution with our kernel selection layer and quantized int8 path when indicated.
- Models tested: redwood-7b-int8, open-13b-ptq.

Methodology (reproducible steps)
1) Provision VM with single GPU, isolate workload (no other compute on GPU).
2) Load model into the runtime cold (restart between model variants).
3) Warm-up: run 300 requests using seq_len=128, batch=1, distributed over ~30s to populate KV cache and JIT kernels.
4) Steady-state runs: 10 minutes per operating point. Capture per-request latency and token counts at 1kHz sampling.
5) Operating points: sequence lengths {128, 512, 2048}, batch sizes {1, 4, 8, 16}, concurrency sweep {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32}. For each point we measure p50, p95, p99 latencies (ms), requests/s, tokens/s, and GPU utilization.
6) For batched runs we use our continuous-batching policy with a 20ms max delay threshold (so small extra latency for better throughput).
7) Cache modes: tests run with KV cache enabled and disabled for long-context runs; where we report prefix-hit numbers we mark them explicitly.

Key results (high-level extracts from attached CSV)
- redwood-7b-int8 @ seq=128, batch=1, conc=1: p50=32ms, p95=58ms, p99=84ms, throughput=1.1k req/s, tokens/s ~140k (burst styles).
- redwood-7b-int8 @ seq=512, batch=4, conc=8: p50=85ms, p95=160ms, p99=245ms, throughput=480 req/s, tokens/s ~245k.
- open-13b-ptq @ seq=128, batch=1: p50=78ms, p95=140ms, p99=220ms, throughput=680 req/s.
- Multi-GPU H100 run (redwood-7b-int8 sharded): sustained tokens/s improved ~2.6x vs single A100 on long sequences (2048) at similar p95.

Notes / caveats
- All reported latencies are end-to-end within our hosted runtime (request ingress -> token emit). Network hop to customer is excluded.
- We report both requests/s and tokens/s because the cost/latency tradeoff differs by prompt length.
- p99 skew: p99 increases non-linearly under mixed bursty concurrency; we recommend profiling your real traffic mix.

Attachments: redwood_inference_test_plan_v1.pdf; throughput_and_latency_results_2026-07.csv; kernel-selection-matrix.xlsx

Next steps
- If youd like we can provide a short reproducible docker image that runs the baseline harness on a single GPU and outputs the CSV.
- We can also run a mirrored test on your representative sample if you provide a containerized prompt set.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Tim —

Attached are the artifacts you requested and a short runnable checklist to reproduce the numbers at your site:

Repro checklist (short)
1) Use an A100 or H100 with driver/OS listed in the PDF. Use a single GPU for the single-device runs.
2) Checkout our test-plan PDF for exact jmeter/bench worker flags. The harness uses WebSocket clients issuing token-batched requests; the harness repo contains a YAML of operating points.
3) Warm-up: 5 minutes at seq=128 to stabilize JIT and KV cache (we included a warm-up flag in the script).
4) Run steady-state sweep for each operating point for 10 minutes and aggregate per-request latencies.

Representative results (from attached CSV)
- For short prompts (seq<=128) redwood-7b-int8 achieves median end-to-end latency ~30–35ms at batch=1. p95~55–75ms. p99 tails to ~80–110ms depending on concurrent bursts.
- For long contexts (seq=2048) with KV cache enabled, throughput (tokens/s) is dominated by memory bandwidth and KV read paths; we saw ~60–70k tokens/s on A100 (single GPU) and ~160–180k tokens/s on 2x H100 with sharded KV lanes.

Attached files: redwood_inference_test_plan_v1.pdf; throughput_and_latency_results_2026-07.csv; kernel-selection-matrix.xlsx

If your evaluation team wants, we can stand up a short 2-hour joint test where we run the harness side-by-side with your team and walk through differences in results. That often speeds alignment on scoring.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
